q: A "paranormal" phenomenon is described as something:
opts: Beyond what is regarded as normal or natural
why: para = beyond + norm = standard → beyond what is normal.

q: The word "resent" can be analyzed in relation to a root associated with:
why: sent = to feel (consent, resent, sentiment).

q: Which root best conveys the idea of "self"?
why: ego = self (egotist, egocentric). mal = bad, dict = say.

q: The semantic relationship between "aquarium" and its root is most closely associated with:
why: aqua = water (aquarium, aquamarine).

q: To "remonstrate" means to protest or object strongly. Its antonym is:
why: Remonstrate = protest, censure. Opposite = acquiesce (accept quietly) / agree.

q: "Concord" most nearly means:
why: Concord = agreement, accord. Antonym: discord.

q: To "quell" a disturbance is to:
why: Quell = subdue, reduce. Antonym: exacerbate, agitate.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to "mollify"?
why: Mollify = appease, assuage → placate. Antonym: irritate, infuriate.

q: Which word best demonstrates the semantic concept behind "dyna"?
why: dyna = power (dynamic, dynamite).

q: "Trenchant" criticism is sharp and incisive. Its antonym is:
why: Trenchant = assertive, forceful, sharp. Antonym: feeble, blunt.

q: Which word best demonstrates the contrast between "pseudo" and authenticity?
why: pseudo = false, not genuine → pseudonym (false name).

q: Which is the closest synonym of "novice"?
why: Novice = tyro, beginner. Antonym: veteran.

q: Which word most clearly demonstrates the root "mort"?
why: mort = death → mortuary. (fort = strength, port = carry, bene = good)

q: A "tyro" is a novice. Its antonym is therefore:
why: Tyro = beginner. Antonym: proficient, veteran.

q: Which word most directly expresses the idea of "hate" through its root?
why: mis/miso = hate → misogyny, misanthrope.

q: "Psychology" is connected to the study of:
why: psycho = soul, mind + logy = study of.

q: The antonym of "morbid" in the sense of unhealthy or diseased is:
why: Morbid = nasty, macabre, unhealthy. Antonym: healthy, cheerful.

q: The root "cide" is most appropriately associated with:
why: cide = killing (homicide, infanticide, patricide).

q: Which word most clearly illustrates the root "fact/fac"?
why: fac/fact = to do, to make (factory, manufacture).

q: A "knave" is most accurately described as:
why: Knave = dishonest person, scoundrel. Antonym: paragon, innocent.

q: An "axiom" is a proposition accepted as self-evident. Which is its closest conceptual opposite?
why: Axiom = adage, truism (self-evident truth). Antonym: absurdity → a doubtful assertion.

q: The antonym of "sublime" in the sense of elevated or noble is:
why: Sublime = magnificent, eminent. Opposite = base (low, ignoble) / ridiculous.

q: In "inscription," the root relationship most strongly suggests:
why: scrib/script = to write (inscription, prescribe).

q: The antonym of "heretic," in a context involving adherence to accepted doctrine, would be:
why: Heretic = non-conformist. Antonym: conformable, religious → orthodoxy adherent.

q: If someone "takes umbrage" at a remark, the person:
why: Umbrage = chagrin, offence. "Take umbrage" = feel offended.

q: A word describing something "unlucky" would most appropriately be associated with:
why: mal = bad, evil (dys = bad/hard/unlucky is not an option). bene, phil, fort are positive.

q: Which is the closest synonym of "vilify"?
why: Vilify = malign, slur, defame. Antonym: cherish, commend.

q: Which word is the closest synonym of "calumny"?
why: Calumny = defamation, aspersion. Antonym: commendation, praise.

q: The root "mit" is most closely associated with:
why: mit = to send (transmit, admit, mission).

q: The word "philanthropy" most directly reflects which underlying idea?
why: phil = love + anthropo = man, humanity.

q: The word "bisection" most directly involves the idea of:
why: bi = two + sect = to cut.

q: "Baroque" is most appropriately associated with something:
why: Baroque = florid, gilt, ornate. Antonym: plain, unadorned.

q: Which word most clearly contains the idea conveyed by "morph"?
why: morph = form, shape (morphing, morphology).

q: The word "synonym" contains a root associated with:
why: nym = name (synonym, antonym, pseudonym).

q: If an argument is "contra" another proposition, it is:
why: contra/counter = against.

q: Which is the best antonym of "languid"?
why: Languid = sluggish, apathetic. Antonym: energetic, spirited.

q: Which word most directly illustrates the root "duc," meaning "to lead"?
why: duc/duct = to lead (conduct, induce).

q: Which root is associated with the concept of "many"?
why: multi = many. mono = one, hypo = below, pseudo = false.

q: A person emerging from a "stupor" would move from a state of:
why: Stupor = lethargy, unconsciousness. Antonym: consciousness, sensibility.

q: The antonym of "insolvent" is:
why: Insolvent = indigent, destitute (bankrupt). Antonym: solvent, wealthy.

q: Which is the strongest antonym of "callous"?
why: Callous = unfeeling, insensitive. Antonym: compassionate, tender.

q: Which word best demonstrates "dict," relating to saying or speaking?
why: dict = to say (dictate, predict, verdict, contradict).

q: If a person is "paralegal," the word formation suggests a relationship to:
why: legal = related to law; paralegal = assists lawyers.

q: Which word most clearly demonstrates "jud," associated with judgment?
why: jud = judge (judicial, prejudice).

q: A "jejune" argument is best described as:
why: Jejune = dull, boring, naive. Antonym: interesting, exciting.

q: "Abject" in the sense of an "abject person" most nearly means:
why: Abject = despicable, servile. Antonym: commendable, praiseworthy.

q: "Circumstance" contains an element suggesting something:
why: circum = around (circumference, circumstance).

q: Which is the closest synonym of "encumbrance"?
why: Encumbrance = hindrance, obstacle → burden. Antonym: incentive.

q: To "rescind" a regulation is to:
why: Rescind = annul, abrogate → revoke. Antonym: permit.

q: Which is the most precise antonym of "obscure" when referring to an idea?
why: Obscure = arcane, vague. Antonym: prominent, clear.

q: The antonym of "vicious" is:
why: Vicious = corrupt, obnoxious. Antonym: noble, virtuous.

q: Which word is the closest synonym of "authentic"?
why: Authentic = accurate, credible → genuine. Antonym: fictitious, unreal.

q: Which word is the strongest synonym for "lax" in the context of discipline?
why: Lax = slack, careless → lenient. Antonym: firm, strict.

q: To "arraign" someone means to:
opts: Call them before a court to answer a charge
why: Arraign = incriminate, indict (charge in court). Antonym: exculpate, pardon.

q: Which root would most appropriately appear in a word describing something "self-directed"?
why: auto = self (automobile, autobiography).

q: A "spectator" is one who:
why: spect = to look (spectator, inspection).

q: The antonym of "imminent" is:
why: Imminent = impending, brewing. Antonym: distant, receding.

q: Which is the strongest antonym of "temperate" in the sense of behaviour?
why: Temperate = cool, moderate. Antonym: boisterous, violent → excessive.

q: Which word is most strongly associated with the root "fract"?
why: fract = to break (fracture, fraction).

q: Which word best demonstrates the root "tele"?
why: tele = far off (telephone, television).

q: Which interpretation of "homogeneous" is most accurate?
opts: Made of similar or uniform elements
why: homo = same (hetero = different).

q: The word "infinitesimal" contains a semantic association with:
why: fin = end, limit; infinitesimal = immeasurably small.

q: Which is the closest antonym of "defray"?
why: Defray = spend, pay (someone's costs). Opposite = impose a cost upon.

q: Which pair is most accurately matched?
why: jud = judge ✓ (port = carry, phil = love, mort = death).

q: Which is the strongest antonym of "clandestine"?
why: Clandestine = covert, furtive. Antonym: open, legal.

q: Which root would be most appropriate for constructing a word meaning "to measure"?
why: metr/meter = measure (thermometer, perimeter).

q: The opposite of "zenith" is:
why: Zenith = summit, apex. Antonym: nadir, base.

q: Which option is the closest synonym of "boisterous"?
why: Boisterous = clamorous, rowdy → tumultuous. Antonym: placid, calm.

q: A term referring to an abnormal or impaired functioning would most logically employ:
why: dys = bad, hard (dysfunctional, dyslexic).

q: Which is the closest antonym of "deride"?
why: Deride = mock, taunt. Antonym: inspire, encourage → commend.

q: Which root most directly conveys the meaning "to look"?
why: vis/vid = to see (vision, video); spect = look. mit = send, cide = kill, form = shape.

q: "Guile" refers to cunning or deceit. Its antonym is:
why: Guile = cunning, deceit. Antonym: honesty, frankness → sincerity.

q: Which word most directly reflects "norm," relating to a standard or rule?
why: norm = typical, standard → normal (paranormal = beyond normal).

q: Which word most clearly exemplifies the root "metr"?
why: metr = measure → geometry (measuring the earth).

q: "Frugality" most nearly means:
why: Frugality = economy, providence → thrift. Antonym: extravagance.

q: Which word most clearly illustrates the root "fort"?
why: fort = strength (fortress, fortitude).

q: Which root most directly means "beneath"?
why: hypo = below, beneath (hypothermia). hyper = above.

q: If a lecture is "insipid," it is most likely:
why: Insipid = tedious, tasteless, vapid → bland. Antonym: pleasing, appetizing.

q: A "squalid" environment is:
why: Squalid = dirty, filthy. Antonym: tidy, attractive.

q: A "quibble" is best described as:
why: Quibble = equivocate, prevaricate → a petty objection.

q: To "concede" a point in an argument is to:
why: Concede = yield, permit. Antonym: deny, reject.

q: A "hapless" individual is:
why: Hapless = unfortunate, ill-fated. Antonym: fortunate, lucky.

q: A "pseudonym" is best understood through the root "nym" as a:
why: pseudo = false + nym = name.

q: To "ratify" an agreement is to:
why: Ratify = consent, approve. Antonym: deny, dissent.

q: Which is the most precise antonym of "lucid" when referring to an explanation?
why: Lucid = sound, rational, clear. Antonym: obscure, hidden.

q: "Subterfuge" is used to achieve an objective through:
why: Subterfuge = deceit, stratagem. Antonym: frankness, openness.

q: Which root is most strongly associated with "death"?
why: mort = death (mortal, mortician).

q: The most appropriate antonym of "immaculate" is:
why: Immaculate = unsullied, spotless. Antonym: defiled, tarnished.

q: In the word "dysfunctional," the root element "dys" most strongly conveys:
why: dys = bad; hard; unlucky → abnormality or difficulty.

q: The root "contra" would most plausibly appear in a word describing:
why: contra = against → opposition (contradict, encounter).

q: Which word most clearly illustrates the root "form"?
why: form = shape (formation, conform, reform).

q: To "efface" something is to erase or obliterate it. Its antonym is:
why: Efface = destroy, obliterate. Antonym: retain, maintain → of these, inscribe (write in).

q: Which root-word pairing is INCORRECT?
why: duc = to LEAD, not writing (scrib = write). Other pairs are correct.

q: A person described as "benevolent" is one whose conduct is primarily:
why: bene = good → benign, generous. Antonym: malevolent.

q: "Televise" contains a root suggesting:
why: tele = far + vis = see.

q: The root "fort" contributes the idea of:
why: fort = strength (fortress, fortitude).

q: Which word best illustrates the meaning of "pater"?
why: pater = father (paternal, paternity). mater = mother.
